user.title: Set up Loxone
user.description: Connect your Miniserver. Below the connection data are the two ways. Way 1 (HA → Loxone) is always active: Home Assistant reads controls and terminals from the Miniserver; its options only decide what gets created. Way 2 (Loxone → HA) is optional: the Miniserver pushes real-time values to Home Assistant over UDP, which changes its program. Previously saved settings are shown here.

data.auto_discovery: Way 1 (HA → Loxone): Discover additional inputs and outputs
data.generate_lightcontroller_subcontrols: Way 1 (HA → Loxone): Show individual lighting circuits
data.edit_room_mapping: Way 1 (HA → Loxone): Assign Loxone rooms to HA areas
data.auto_configure_udp: Way 2 (Loxone → HA): Set up real-time values over UDP automatically
data.udp_port: Way 2 (Loxone → HA): UDP receiving port in Home Assistant
data.udp_max_signals: Way 1 (HA → Loxone): Maximum number of additionally discovered terminals

data_description.username: User Home Assistant uses to sign in to the Miniserver.
data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Miniserver, e.g. 192.168.1.10.
data_description.port: Usually 80 for HTTP or 443 for HTTPS.
data_description.auto_discovery: Also finds physical inputs and outputs that are not enabled for visualization in Loxone and adds them to HA.
data_description.generate_lightcontroller_subcontrols: Adds the individual circuits of a Loxone lighting controller as separate HA entities. Lighting moods are always available as effects of the light entity, independent of this option.
data_description.edit_room_mapping: Opens another dialog after you confirm this form. Match a Loxone room to an existing Home Assistant area. Existing manual assignments are preserved.
data_description.auto_configure_udp: The Miniserver reports changes of the additionally discovered inputs and outputs to HA immediately. This backs up and changes the Miniserver program and briefly restarts its logic. Use at your own risk, see the disclaimer in the documentation. When off, values are polled every 30 seconds, or you configure the UDP logger manually.
data_description.udp_port: Usually leave at 55555. Set to 0 to disable UDP reception. For manual setup, use the same destination port on the Miniserver.
data_description.udp_max_signals: Limits how many discovered terminals are created as entities and updated by polling or UDP, in program order. Protects the Miniservers, the network and Home Assistant on very large installations such as Gateway/Client systems. A log message tells you when the limit is reached.

room_mapping.title: Assign Loxone rooms to HA areas
room_mapping.description: Choose a Home Assistant area for each Loxone room. Existing mappings are preselected. Leave a selection empty for no mapping. Use X to remove a saved mapping; devices retain their previous placement. Confirm once to save the whole list. Manual area assignments still take precedence.

error.room_fetch_failed: Rooms could not be loaded. Check connectivity and Loxone access, or skip optional room mapping.
error.invalid_area: Select an existing Home Assistant area.

reload.name: Pyloxone Reload
reload.description: Reloads the Loxone integration by reconnecting to the Miniserver and refreshing all entities. This is useful after making configuration changes in Loxone Config or when connection issues occur. All current entity states will be re\-synchronized from the Miniserver.

event_websocket_command.name: Send Websocket command
event_websocket_command.description: Send websocket commands to the loxone server. You can send a command to the Miniserver using an entity or using a UUID. If you specify both, the command will be sent to the Entity. More info and commands can be found on the Loxone Website
